solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: A route out of India? Unlikely, in such peaceful surroundings (4,4,2,3)

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO alphabet
unlikely, as in a tall story

annotation.surface: A traveller wonders whether any road could lead out of India to somewhere this tranquil.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: 'A route out of India' looks like one travel phrase but is four pieces, and TALL means unlikely as in a tall tale.
annotation.definitionFit: To be away from it all is to be somewhere quiet, far from the bustle of everyday life.

entries.clue: Play or plaything (1,5,5)

blocks.note: a drama for the stage, here Ibsen's best-known one

annotation.walkthrough: Ibsen's 1879 drama and the children's toy share a name, so the two definitions hang on the near-echo of play and plaything.
annotation.definitionFit: A Doll's House is Ibsen's play, and a doll's house is a miniature house children play with.

entries.clue: Jack’s parted from brisk relative (5)

indicatorNotes.parted from: Jack is separated from the word, so its J goes

blocks.note: J marks the jack on a playing card, and this is the letter parted from the word; the ’s is 'is'

annotation.surface: A man called Jack has fallen out with a lively member of the family.
annotation.walkthrough: Jack reads as a man's name; here it is only the letter J, taken away from JAUNTY.
annotation.definitionFit: An aunty is the familiar form of aunt, your parent's sister, and so a relative by example.

entries.clue: Making sense of plump sort of pigeon (9)

annotation.surface: Someone is trying to work out what kind of pigeon a fat one might be.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plump sort of pigeon' reads as one description of a single bird, but plump and the pigeon's kind are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Fathoming something is getting to the bottom of it, making sense of it.

entries.clue: Rich old university cushioned by endless wealth (7)

indicatorNotes.cushioned by: the university sits padded inside the wealth

annotation.surface: A privileged old university sits cosily wrapped in bottomless riches.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rich old university' reads as one phrase about an Oxbridge college; 'Rich' alone is the definition, and 'old' is a separate letter placed in front.
annotation.definitionFit: Opulent is a plain synonym for rich, often of lavish surroundings or display.

entries.clue: Order for building barrio nice houses (5)

indicatorNotes.houses: the phrase contains the answer within it

annotation.surface: A planning order allows new building in a pleasant Spanish-speaking neighbourhood.
annotation.walkthrough: A barrio is a Spanish-speaking district. The Ionic order is one of the classical styles of column, so an order for building is architectural, not a planning permit.
annotation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture.

entries.clue: Cleared a cold and departed (9)

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Someone got over a cold and then went on their way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cleared a cold' reads as recovering from illness; 'Cleared' is the definition, in its courtroom sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A defendant who is acquitted is cleared of the charge.

entries.clue: First to see down solution (3)

indicatorNotes.First to: the first letter of the see is moved
indicatorNotes.down: in a down entry, going down means moving to the bottom

blocks.note: Ely, the cathedral city whose bishop's see is a crossword regular

annotation.surface: An instruction to be first to look down at the answer.
annotation.walkthrough: The first letter of ELY drops to the bottom, giving LYE. A see is a bishop's diocese, and Ely is the stock one.
annotation.definitionFit: Lye is an alkaline solution used in cleaning and soap-making.

entries.clue: On radio, grumble is cut (4)

indicatorNotes.On radio: what is heard on the radio is only sound

annotation.surface: A complaint made over the airwaves is edited out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as a broadcast being censored; here it is a lawn being mown.
annotation.definitionFit: Mown is the past participle of mow, used of grass or hay that has been cut with a blade.

entries.clue: Our quintet is playing, but this stops the flow (10)

indicatorNotes.is playing: the letters are performed in a new order

annotation.surface: A band announces its five players are performing, yet something halts the music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The flow' sounds like the flow of the music the quintet plays; it is the flow of blood.
annotation.definitionFit: A tourniquet is a band tightened round a limb to stop bleeding.

entries.clue: Hacker stood less on ceremony at first (8)

indicatorNotes.at first: only the first letter of ceremony is used
indicatorNotes.on: LAY MORE comes on after C

blocks.note: if you lay more, you stood less

annotation.surface: A computer hacker was less formal to begin with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hacker' looks like a computer intruder; it is a sword that hacks. LAY is the past of lie, the opposite of stood.
annotation.definitionFit: A claymore is a large Scottish broadsword, a weapon for hacking.

entries.clue: Child’s play receives large hug (6)

blocks.note: a cinch = something easy, child's play

annotation.surface: A child playing gets a big cuddle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Child’s play' reads as a child's game; it means something easy.
annotation.definitionFit: A clinch is a boxer's or lovers' close hold, so a tight embrace; hug is the everyday word for it.

entries.clue: Romance will flourish, as with Oliver (11)

indicatorNotes.flourish: the letters are waved about into a new shape

annotation.surface: A prediction that love will blossom, just as it did for someone called Oliver.
annotation.walkthrough: Oliver looks like a romantic hero; he is Oliver Cromwell, the Puritan who ruled England in the 1650s.
annotation.definitionFit: Cromwellian means relating to Oliver Cromwell.

entries.clue: One criminal to turn in another? About time (10)

indicatorNotes.About: About means around, so the lifer's letters are placed around the time.

blocks.note: to shop someone is to inform on them
a lifer, another criminal, serving a life sentence

annotation.surface: One crook wonders about grassing on another, and decides it is about time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second criminal, a LIFER, which then goes round T.
annotation.definitionFit: A shoplifter is a criminal who steals from shops.

entries.clue: Each app fails with Charlie irate (3,6)

indicatorNotes.fails: the letters break down and are rebuilt

blocks.note: C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Every time an app crashes, a man called Charlie loses his temper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Each' looks like part of the story about the app; it is the definition, as in a price per head.
annotation.definitionFit: Per capita is Latin for by heads, used of figures reckoned for each person, as in income per capita.

entries.clue: Phone and receiver clearly separate (4-5)

annotation.surface: A phone and its handset come apart cleanly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' sounds like the phone handset; it is a receiver of stolen goods.
annotation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money or land is to mark it off clearly, keeping it separate.

entries.clue: Did work against sanction (4)

blocks.note: against = to, as in shoulder to shoulder
to sanction is to approve, and the two-letter word of approval is used here

annotation.surface: Someone worked in defiance of a penalty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' looks like a penalty; it means approval. 'Did work' is the sense in which a graft or a vaccination took.
annotation.definitionFit: A graft or a dye that took worked as intended.

entries.clue: Car manufacturer lacking agreement from German plant (4)

indicatorNotes.lacking: the car name is missing the German yes

annotation.surface: A carmaker has no deal with a German factory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory, to go with the carmaker; it is a botanical plant. Guar is a bean grown for guar gum.
annotation.definitionFit: Guar is a leguminous plant cultivated for its seeds.

entries.clue: Earth and hill reduced to dust? (6,4)

blocks.note: a down is a rolling chalk hill, as in the South Downs

annotation.surface: Soil and a hillside worn away to powder.
annotation.walkthrough: A down is a low grassy hill in southern England.
annotation.definitionFit: Something ground down has been crushed to powder, reduced to dust.

entries.clue: Gold tooth perhaps rounder (7)

blocks.note: a tooth is one thing that bites

annotation.surface: A gold tooth might be more curved than the rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rounder' looks like a comparative of round; it is one who goes round, an orbiter.
annotation.definitionFit: An orbiter circles a planet, so it is something that goes round.

entries.clue: Meal is about over (6)

annotation.surface: Dinner is nearly finished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About over' reads as nearly finished; it splits into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Repast is a formal, rather literary word for a meal, from Old French repaistre, to feed.

entries.clue: In alternation, two preach Jewish law (5)

indicatorNotes.In alternation: Things in alternation take turns, so the letters kept and the letters skipped take turns along the phrase.

annotation.surface: Two people take turns preaching on Jewish law.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two preach' looks like a pair of speakers; the letters T-O-R-A-H alternate through it.
annotation.definitionFit: The Torah is the body of Jewish law, the first five books of the Hebrew Bible.

entries.clue: Perplex crowd wanting leader to pursue expeditionary force (8)

indicatorNotes.wanting leader: HUDDLE is without its first letter
indicatorNotes.to pursue: To pursue something is to go after it, so the crowd's letters come after the force's.

blocks.note: HUDDLE, a crowd, without its H

annotation.surface: A headless mob bewilders an army as it chases after it.
annotation.walkthrough: The BEF was the British army sent to France in both world wars.
annotation.definitionFit: To befuddle is to muddle someone's thinking, a plain synonym for perplex.

entries.clue: Following doctor’s lead, I almost choose to get lump removed (5)

indicatorNotes.Following: What follows comes after, so the rest is placed after the doctor's letter.
indicatorNotes.lead: only the leading letter of doctor

annotation.surface: A patient follows the doctor's advice and chooses to have a lump cut out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lump removed' reads as surgery; a divot is turf gouged out by a golf club.
annotation.definitionFit: A divot is a chunk of turf removed by a club stroke.

entries.clue: Very small thing inhibiting professional heavyweight? (10)

blocks.note: a ton is a heavy weight

annotation.surface: A tiny rule stops a heavyweight boxer from turning professional.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavyweight' looks like a boxer; it is just a TON. The question mark flags the joke of something so tiny hiding a heavyweight.
annotation.definitionFit: An antiproton is the antimatter twin of the proton, a subatomic particle and so a very small thing by example.

entries.clue: Have to get name promoted immediately (3)

indicatorNotes.promoted: in a down entry, the N moves up to the top

blocks.note: N = name, the last letter of OWN already, and the one moved

annotation.surface: An urgent need to get someone's name moved up the list straight away.
annotation.walkthrough: The N at the end of OWN is promoted to the top of this down entry, giving NOW.
annotation.definitionFit: Now in the sense of at once, as in 'do it now', is a plain synonym for immediately.

entries.clue: Empty vessel in the sound (4)

indicatorNotes.in the sound: In the sound means as the word is heard, not as it is spelt, so a word with the same sound is wanted.

blocks.note: a vein is a blood vessel

annotation.surface: An empty ship lies out in the sound, a stretch of sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'sound' suggest a ship at sea; the vessel is a vein and the sound is the ear's.
annotation.definitionFit: Vain as in empty and futile: a vain threat or promise.

entries.clue: Affected by exposure, wife collapsing beneath a tree (7-6)

indicatorNotes.collapsing: the letters fall into a new order

annotation.surface: A woman out in the elements collapses under a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface is a scene of weather damage, so the definition and the story overlap.
annotation.definitionFit: Weather-beaten means worn and marked by exposure to the elements.
